A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 27-page versions of the same EmotionThinker paper. The main text, equations, tables, figures, references and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original emotion-recognition experiments, reasoning-quality evaluations, human ratings, ablations and sensitivity analyses in Section 4, plus model-output comparisons in Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons, human evaluations, ablations and appendix case-study outputs.

M1.justification: The EmotionThinker procedure is unchanged: prosody-centric supervised fine-tuning, cold-start reasoning supervision and GRPO-PTR with progressive reasoning rewards and trustworthiness weighting. Sections 3 and Appendices B–D introduce no procedural or architectural changes.

E1.justification: Training sources and task coverage are unchanged. Both versions evaluate IEMOCAP, MELD, RAVDESS and SAVEE, along with the same prosody-perception test and human reasoning assessment.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same 16 comparison models. Comparator membership is also unchanged in the human evaluation, training-strategy ablations and appendix case study.

E3.justification: The train/test and zero-shot settings, evaluation metrics, training budgets, model configurations and human-assessment protocol are unchanged. Table 7 retains exactly the same tested reward-weight settings.

E4.justification: The reward-weight sensitivity evidence in Table 7 is corrected: the revised average makes alpha_t = 0.5 rank above alpha_t = 0.3. This is a limited revision within an existing analysis; the tested settings, other ablations, prosody analysis and case studies are unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting practices are unchanged. Both versions retain point-estimate reporting and the same four-reviewer human assessment, with no added seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 7 changes the average for alpha_o = 1.0, alpha_t = 0.5 from 66.89 to 68.89. Its four per-dataset scores remain unchanged, and 68.89 matches the existing result in Table 2. All other numerical results and qualitative outputs, including the appendices, are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 retains identical reward definitions, score normalization, response-group definitions, trustworthiness weighting and combined-reward mathematics. No assumptions, proofs or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: EmotionCoT-35K, prosody-enhanced EmotionThinker-Base and GRPO-PTR, together with the same claims about recognition accuracy and explainable emotion reasoning.

C2.justification: The discussion already favored alpha_t = 0.5 in v1 and retains that interpretation in v2. Explanations of prosody enhancement, reward-model quality, trust weighting and progressive scheduling are unchanged; no substantive limitations or applicability qualifications are added.

D1.justification: Implementation details, training hyperparameters, data-construction instructions, prompts and project-access information are unchanged. Appendix text crossing different page boundaries is retained content, not newly disclosed technical information.

R1.justification: Section 2, the cited works and the complete reference list are unchanged. The positioning relative to previous speech-emotion and multimodal-reasoning research is retained.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 6, Acknowledgement, describing CPII/InnoHK funding support, and adds its contents entry. The arXiv version/date stamp is updated; the scientific narrative is otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 7 corrects IEMOCAP best-score highlighting from 77.68 at alpha_t = 0.5 to 77.71 at alpha_t = 0.3. The acknowledgement and contents addition also cause limited reflow on pages 15–18. No figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: The Table 7 correction resolves an inconsistency with Table 2 and the existing conclusion favoring alpha_t = 0.5. Corrected IEMOCAP highlighting also improves reporting accuracy, while the acknowledgement adds funding disclosure. These are limited improvements in consistency and transparency; the scientific methods and broader evidence remain unchanged.
